claims.text: Controlled cooling and mild annealing will induce nanoscale phase segregation in the high-entropy alloy.
Nanoscale phase segregation will enhance local electron–phonon coupling.
Enhanced local electron–phonon coupling will enable Cooper-pair formation.
Cooper-pair formation will lead to superconductivity at low temperature.
The as-fabricated alloy is predominantly homogeneous and lacks intentionally induced microstructural inhomogeneities.
The cooling and annealing protocol can promote nanoscale phase segregation while preserving overall alloy composition.
Nano-domains or grain-boundary regions generated by segregation contain lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions in the segregated regions enhance electron–phonon interactions.
The pairing-enhancing mechanism is absent in the uniform as-fabricated state.
The annealed alloy will exhibit zero electrical resistance below a critical temperature.
The annealed alloy will exhibit a measurable Meissner effect below a critical temperature.
The homogeneous as-fabricated control will not exhibit superconductivity under identical low-temperature conditions.
The untreated as-fabricated alloy does not display superconductivity under the specified low-temperature conditions.
The proposed mechanism should apply only when processing produces detectable nanoscale segregation.
Changes in composition, processing, or contamination that prevent nano-domain formation can limit the mechanism.
